correctness.rationale: A shuffle π-square of an even ternary length-eight word is witnessed by one of 70 four-position subsequences and a complementary length-four subsequence satisfying either alignment direction. π and π^(-1) have the same neighborhood, yielding 17 inverse classes of S4. All 1641 even ternary length-eight words reduce by alphabet relabeling to 274 canonical words (1 one-symbol +63 two-symbol +210 three-symbol). An independently coded direct compatibility predicate checked all 1641 and confirmed that the seven proposed permutations [1234,1342,2143,2314,2431,3241,3421] cover all, with incremental canonical counts [104,76,29,34,18,9,4]. It separately recomputed complete inverse-class compatible sets of seven lower-bound words 00001122,00001221,00011022,00011220,00012210,01221000,01222210; the respective sets were {1234,2134},{1243,2143},{1324,2314},{1342,2341},{1432,2431},{3214,3241},{3421,4231,4321}, pairwise disjoint. Thus any covering uses ≥7 inverse classes and the proposed family has size7. Exhaustive finite certificate is an exact proof for the fixed finite domain, with no extension asserted to other half-lengths.

The first ternary half-length-four off-diagonal m3(4), accompanied by independent matching upper and lower certificates, is a natural finite cutoff and precise parameter a researcher studying shuffle coverings can directly use. It does not claim a paper-sized or all-length theorem.
